definition: Handedness is the greater skill or dominance of one hand over the other. In this historical source, the usual form is right-handedness, while left-handedness is described as the less common opposite and contrasted with ambidextrous ability in both hands.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Ambidextrous; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not directly define “handedness” as “greater skill or dominance of one hand over the other”; it only characterizes “ambidextrous” as equal or nearly equal facility and contrasts it with “normal superiority of the right hand” and “exceptional superiority of the left-hand.”
The definition claims that left-handedness is “the less common opposite”; the packet does not state frequency or commonness for left-handedness (it only says “exceptional superiority”).

The definition’s framing is derived from an “ambidextrous” entry rather than a handedness entry; the packet supports contrast between ambidextrous and right/left superiority, but not the requested standalone definition of handedness.
